# Results (generated by `pipeline/05_summary.py` - do not edit by hand)

Objective, all stages: k=20 seeds, weighted (p_uv = c / max(followees(v), 1)) cascade on the Higgs FOLLOWER graph (WCC, 456,290 nodes / 14,855,466 edges, followee -> follower), parameter 0.4931 calibrated on the real activity log (see validation/); 80 sims per evaluation; winners re-evaluated with 400 fresh sims.

Shared baselines: top-degree **23462.9** (4000 sims; 30x150-sim reps: 23486.4 ± 289.9); random seeds 31.8 ± 10.3.

## Stage-specific controls

- **Heuristics (stage 1):** Top-degree 23462.9, Top-PageRank 32884.7, Top-k-core 8020.7, Random seeds 31.8.
- **CELF (stage 2):** lazy greedy on 200 fixed live-edge snapshots over the top-3000 out-degree pool; snapshot estimate 33990.0, fresh 400-sim 34032.7 (+45.05% vs top-degree; set-level t=187.76, p=2.8e-55); shares 18/20 seeds with top-degree.
- **Decoder-only (stage 4):** z=0 (no BO bias), diversity weight swept on an 11-point grid; best fresh 23336.3 (-0.54% vs top-degree; set-level p=0.31). BO runs above decoder-only: 4/5.
- **Stage 3 pool:** 1497 embedded nodes; 20/20 top-degree seeds are inside it.

## How to read the p-values

The set-level Welch test compares Monte Carlo estimates of two *fixed* seed sets. It supports "this particular seed set spreads more/less than top-degree", not "BO beats top-degree". Method-level evidence is the run-level columns: mean ± sd across independent BO runs and how many runs beat top-degree.
